_: indonesian-fixes.json — every hand edit to an Indonesian deck of card type ukbi, applied by indonesian-fix.js after .claude/ukbi/run.py (its header has the format). Nothing in it is composed: a meaning is a gloss of the English Wiktionary (via kaikki.org, the extraction fetched on 2026-11-19) with the register its sense is tagged with in brackets as the dictionary prints it, a root is the base its etymology or its head line names, a sentence is a Tatoeba sentence named by id. A cut is said to be a cut in its why.

ukbi1.subtitle: {notes} words · start here: level 1 of 7 · both directions, as two cards per word
ukbi1.lead: START HERE if you have no Indonesian. This is the first of eight decks on the shelf, studied in the order UKBI 1 to UKBI 7 and then the phrases, with the short deck Indonesian — Sounds and spelling beside this one. UKBI is a proficiency test and not a course: its lowest predicate, Terbatas, is level 1 here, and this deck is the survival vocabulary that predicate describes. THE ORDER: the first {day:sebuah} days are a head written by hand — the courtesies (halo, terima kasih and sama-sama on day {day:halo}, selamat pagi and apa kabar on day {day:selamat pagi}, maaf and permisi on day {day:maaf}), the parts of the day, I and you (saya, aku, Anda, kamu on day {day:saya}), siapa and nama, here and there, the commonest verbs from day {day:mau}, the aspect words and the negations (sudah and belum on day {day:sudah}, jangan on day {day:jangan}), the question words from day {day:kapan}, and nol to sepuluh on days {day:nol} to {day:sepuluh}. After it the commonest words come first, with the numbers above ten dealt as one run from day {day:sebelas}, the days of the week from day {day:Senin}, the colours from day {day:warna} and the months from day {day:Januari}, and no derived word before its root. THE PACE: the default is ten new cards a day, and a word is two cards, so five words a day. The deck takes {days} days; UKBI 2 begins on day {start:ukbi2} of the shelf, UKBI 3 on day {start:ukbi3}, UKBI 4 on day {start:ukbi4}, and the eight decks together are {shelfNotes} words, {shelfDays} days, {shelfYears} years. A deck cannot set its own limit: raise it in the deck's options to go faster. WHAT THE CARDS SHOW OF THE GRAMMAR, since no deck explains it. Register: saya (polite) and aku (informal) are both I, Anda (formal) and kamu (informal) both you, and each card says which in brackets as the dictionary does; kau, which the shelf's example sentences use for you, carries the dictionary's own label; kita is we with the listener and kami we without. Negation: tidak (its card says verbs, adverbs and adjectives), bukan (its three sentences each negate a noun), belum (not yet) and jangan (don't) are four cards. Time: a verb has no tenses, and sudah, sedang, akan, belum, masih and pernah are cards dealt together. Building words: a Forms row names a word's root and, where the dictionary names it, the affix it is built with (meng-, ber-, ter-, ke- -an, -an); how meng- changes with its root, the word written twice (hati-hati), and -ku, -mu and -nya written onto a word (namamu, your name) are cards of the sounds deck: many sentences carry a form with -ku, -mu or -nya and no Forms row shows one. {inserted} of the {notes} are not the generator's and were put in by hand in November 2026: kau is new, with its meaning from the English Wiktionary and its sentences from Tatoeba; dari mana and yang mana came down from UKBI 2, tidak apa-apa from UKBI 3, selamat jalan and selamat makan from the phrases deck. —
